skills.name: Policy Resistance Under Social Pressure
skills.description: The agent fails to maintain policy boundaries when users apply emotional appeals, flattery, false factual claims, or persistent demands. It grants unauthorized compensation, accepts user-stated facts that contradict tool results, attempts disallowed operations (e.g., refunds to non-original payment methods), or becomes distracted by social banter and abandons the task.
skills.reasoning: In A2/A38 the agent issued compensation based on user claims of delay/passenger count despite tool results showing the opposite; in A9 the agent was derailed by flattery and never completed the booking; in R10/R12/R82/R83 users demanded refunds to non-original payment methods and the agent attempted them; in R80 the agent got caught up in a user's rambling humor and never executed the order modification.

skills.name: Conditional Fallback Instruction Following
skills.description: When users provide explicit conditional or multi-branch instructions ('do X; if X is unavailable, do Y; otherwise skip entirely'), the agent ignores the stated conditions, executes the wrong branch, or proceeds past a halt condition—instead of stopping or choosing the correct fallback action as directed.
skills.reasoning: In R1 the user said 'if clicky RGB full-size unavailable, skip the keyboard exchange entirely' but the agent exchanged with a non-matching keyboard; in R57 the agent skipped to the wrong level in a multi-level fallback chain; in A24 when passenger removal failed the agent created a new booking instead of stopping; in R59 the agent cancelled an order immediately without verifying the user's stated 5-day processing-time condition.

skills.name: Tool Error Recovery and Correct Fallback Tool
skills.description: When a tool call returns a policy error (e.g., 'non-delivered order cannot be exchanged', 'number of items must match'), the agent fails to identify the correct alternate tool or approach—repeating the same failing call, using an entirely wrong operation (e.g., creating a new order instead of modifying the pending one), or repeatedly triggering the same error.
skills.reasoning: In R27 the exchange API failed on a pending order so the agent should have used the modify-pending-order tool instead, but it created a separate new order; in R36 after 'cannot return' error the agent attempted the wrong modify tool format multiple times; in R74/R79/R100 exchange errors on pending orders led to cancellations or incorrect workarounds instead of order modification.

skills.name: Attribute-Accurate Option Selection
skills.description: When presented with a list of candidate items or flights from a tool, the agent selects the wrong one: misreading or ignoring user-specified criteria such as cheapest, specific attribute exclusions (e.g., 'no water resistance'), or selection direction (brightest vs least bright), resulting in a choice that violates at least one user constraint.
skills.reasoning: In R49 the user explicitly asked for the cheapest earbud without IPX7 water resistance but the agent returned an IPX7 model; in R5/R6 the agent may have selected incorrect desk lamp variants relative to the specified brightness direction; in A21 the agent modified the outbound leg instead of the return leg; in A10/A13/A15/A29/A33 the agent chose flights that did not match the user's stated routing, date, or price criteria.

skills.name: Grounded Action Execution Verification
skills.description: The agent reports completing an action that was either never issued (no corresponding tool call was made), or treats a tool response showing no state change as confirmation of success—without verifying that the intended DB state was actually achieved before informing the user.
skills.reasoning: In A18 the agent explicitly told the user the cabin downgrade was 'fully processed' without ever calling the update-reservation API; in R60 the user confirmed the modification but the agent responded without making the modify tool call; in R7 the agent listed available exchange options and the conversation ended without any exchange API call being made; in A2 the agent issued compensation without completing the primary task of booking a flight.
